# Nested corpus requests

Full pinned Django remains the benchmark. Subsets are optional diagnostics, never a required ladder or separate success targets; no subset execution is scheduled.

`prepare.py` creates existing `run-ryo` request templates and a sealed input plan without invoking either worker. It accepts the already-pinned corpus inventory, frozen profile, request settings, native collector and baseline worker receipt. All source bytes are verified before preparation. The output contains nested 100/500/1000/full file lists, exact file order and source hashes, phase/module settings, fixed worker policy and predeclared per-process caps.

Each prefix starts with the four measured Django tail files, ten largest files, lexical endpoints and the known syntax fixture. Remaining files interleave source families and byte-size quartiles in deterministic hash order. This deliberately includes expensive tails; it is not a random population estimate.

Before execution, seal the candidate, verify all input hashes again, and run a small preflight. Materialize a separate request with a unique absent enabled cache path for every invocation. Use the existing native collector, and admit successful reports through `verify_profiles.complete_run_ryo_report` with exact settings. Compare entire canonical reports, including file inventory, coverage and skip receipts, before considering wall/CPU/RSS. Preserve both raw outputs, load/process overlap, signal termination and censored observations. Equal failures never establish equivalence. Large capped observations do not establish a completed scaling slope.

These requests initially measure a new process with cold tool state. OS cache remains uncontrolled. The existing CLI benchmark also supports retained-tool-cache repetitions and deterministic edited-tool-cache runs in separate processes. Its edited results are checked against fresh-cache executions for each contestant; this does not require a new persistent transport. Retained paths do not establish verified cache hits. Same-session warm engine state is an optional separate metric and must not be inferred from warmed filesystem pages or separate processes.
